generatedProse.practice-connection:
Everything in this course applies to the work you are already doing. Analysis, evaluation and synthesis are the engine of academic work: every essay that asks you to evaluate a theory, every review that draws sources together, every seminar where interpretations are weighed, runs on these three skills. Treat what follows as being about your own essays and reading, not about study in the abstract.

The same habit carries into working life. Wherever you are given evidence, asked to judge it, and expected to argue a case, the people whose work improves are those who take it apart, weigh it, and build from it. The critical skills you practise here are ones you keep long after you graduate.
